item.title: ‘I warned Lloyds Metals’: Maru
item.description: The National Government and the country must not be blamed for the attack at the Lloyds Metals & Energy Limited’s camp in Panguna at the Autonomous Region of Bougainville, says the Minister for International Trade and Investment, Richard Maru. “I repeatedly advised the management of Lloyds Metals & Energy against investing in Panguna, knowing it was highly volatile due to numerous factions and the
item.content:encoded:
The National Government and the country must not be blamed for the attack at the Lloyds Metals & Energy Limited’s camp in Panguna at the Autonomous Region of Bougainville, says the Minister for International Trade and Investment, Richard Maru.

“I repeatedly advised the management of Lloyds Metals & Energy against investing in Panguna, knowing it was highly volatile due to numerous factions and the environment was not conducive for investment," Maru said in a media statement.

"I feared the very outcome that has now transpired. Despite my advice, the company took a decision to invest in Panguna and it must now accept full responsibility for what has happened. They took it upon themselves not to heed National Government advice."

The Lloyds Metals & Energy Limited is a significant player in India’s metals and mining sector. According to the reports from Bougainville, heavy machinery and vehicles reportedly belonging to the company were destroyed in an arson attack at the Panguna mine site yesterday morning.

“I strongly condemn this attack in the strongest possible terms as the Minister responsible for international trade and investment," Maru said.

"I do appreciate that many things were not sorted out like the landowner issues. I am saddened by what has happened but as the Minster responsible, I had done my part by advising the Lloyds Metals & Energy against this investment because it was risky and I foresaw what was coming,” said Minister Maru.

“I call on the Government and people of the Autonomous Region of Bougainville to deal with those involved in this attack if they are serious about attracting investments into the region."

item.title: New hangar at Balimo airstrip to boost services
item.description: A new K9.2 million aircraft hangar was officially opened at Balimo Airstrip today, aimed at strengthening aviation services in Western province. The facility, funded by the Sustainable Development Program [SDP], was built between June 2024 and 2026. It includes a modern aircraft hangar, an aircraft fuel shed, and two aircraft parking bays.
item.content:encoded:
A new K9.2 million aircraft hangar was officially opened at Balimo Airstrip today, aimed at strengthening aviation services in Western province.

The facility, funded by the Sustainable Development Program [SDP], was built between June 2024 and 2026. It includes a modern aircraft hangar, an aircraft fuel shed, and two aircraft parking bays.

SDP says the completion of the hangar is critical to supporting the safe operation and maintenance of MAF aircraft, which provide vital services to communities across Western.

These services include transporting students and teachers of Balimo College, freight such as vegetables, and the delivery of essential medical services through SDP’s Aerial Health Patrol program, including emergency medevacs.

MAF is SDP’s aviation partner and operator based in Balimo. MAF has been providing critical air services in the region since it first established a base at nearby Wasua in 1962.

The new hangar will now house MAF’s regional operations, including aircraft, equipment, passenger handling facilities and an office. It also provides shelter for two airplanes and a safe place for engineering and maintenance work.

SDP chief executive officer Lesieli Taviri said the investment reflects SDP’s commitment to strengthening infrastructure that improves service delivery in Western Province.

“Investments in aviation infrastructure are investments in people. They improve access to healthcare, education, markets and emergency services while helping ensure communities remain connected and supported," Taviri said.

Dom Sant, Country Director of MAF in PNG said the Balimo airstrip serves as a critical gateway for the Delta and Middle Fly districts.

“The MAF hangar and surrounding aviation facilities funded by SDP plays a vital role in enabling MAF’s services throughout Western Province including SDP’s aerial health patrols and community development programs," Sant said.

SDP thanked the Western Provincial and District level government for their continued support in improving aviation services for the people.

item.title: Fatal Vanimo crash triggers major traffic enforcement operation in West Sepik
item.description: West Sepik Police are preparing to launch a major traffic enforcement operation following a fatal road accident that claimed the lives of a young couple along the Vanimo-Wutung Highway on Sunday. The couple died after the motorcycle they were travelling on collided with a Toyota Land Cruiser along the Ilolo section of the highway between 11am and midday on September 13.
item.content:encoded:
West Sepik Police are preparing to launch a major traffic enforcement operation following a fatal road accident that claimed the lives of a young couple along the Vanimo-Wutung Highway on Sunday.

The couple died after the motorcycle they were travelling on collided with a Toyota Land Cruiser along the Ilolo section of the highway between 11am and midday on September 13.

According to police, the couple were returning towards their village and were carrying a birthday cake for their daughter when the collision occurred.

Both the motorcycle rider and his wife died at the scene.

Police have since arrested and detained a 24-year-old man in connection with the accident. West Sepik Provincial Police Commander, Senior Inspector Silas Kuiano, says investigations are continuing to establish the full circumstances surrounding the crash.

He has appealed to relatives of the deceased, residents of Lido and nearby villages, and the wider Vanimo community to remain calm and allow police investigators to carry out their work.

“This is a tragic loss of two young lives, and we understand the pain and grief being experienced by their families and community,” Senior Inspector Kuiano said.

He said any charges arising from the investigation would be dealt with through the proper legal process. The fatal crash has also prompted renewed concern from West Sepik Police over road safety, particularly the growing number of motorcycles operating across the province.

PPC Kuiano says the increasing use of motorcycles has been accompanied by a rise in serious and fatal road accidents involving motorcycle riders.

As a result, West Sepik Police will commence a major traffic enforcement operation targeting motorists and motorcycle riders who breach traffic laws.

The operation will target: • Unregistered and uninsured motorcycles • Unlicensed motorcycle riders and motor vehicle drivers • Vehicles and motorcycles without valid roadworthiness certificates • Driving or riding under the influence of alcohol • Dangerous, careless and reckless driving or riding • Other serious breaches of traffic laws

Police will work with relevant transport and road safety authorities to strengthen compliance and reduce preventable deaths on West Sepik roads.

The PPC has also reminded vehicle owners, drivers and motorcycle riders to ensure their vehicles are properly registered, insured and roadworthy, and that they hold valid licences.

He is urging all road users to exercise greater caution, observe speed limits and wear approved safety helmets.

Motorists and motorcycle riders have also been warned against unsafe practices, including carrying passengers or operating vehicles and motorcycles unsafely.

The latest crash adds to growing concern over road deaths along the Vanimo-Wutung Highway, with four reported road deaths recorded over the past two months.

Police say stronger regulation, compliance and enforcement will be necessary as motorcycle use continues to increase in the province.

PPC Kuiano says the relevant authorities should also review arrangements governing the importation, registration and licensing of motorcycles entering and operating in West Sepik.

“Road safety is everyone’s responsibility,” the PPC said, warning that one careless decision on the road can destroy lives and leave families and communities dealing with lasting grief.

item.title: Madang police launch five-day independence operation
item.description: Madang police have launched a five-day special operation to secure the province’s 51st Independence Anniversary celebrations, coinciding with the command's third-quarter parade. The operation, which runs from today through Friday, saw a strong turnout of personnel from across the province’s districts.
item.content:encoded:
Madang police have launched a five-day special operation to secure the province’s 51st Independence Anniversary celebrations, coinciding with the command's third-quarter parade.

The operation, which runs from today through Friday, saw a strong turnout of personnel from across the province’s districts.

Addressing the parade, Provincial Police Commander [PPC] Superintendent Robert Baim stressed the critical need for teamwork, discipline, and unity across all sections of the force during the celebration period.

"This is no time to waste and to play around. This year is the first year of the next 50 years for this country," Supt Baim said.

"For this operation, I want us to put aside our differences and operate as a team, not section by section or as individuals. We will work together in oneness, in one spirit as a team, and as one Royal PNG Constabulary (RPNGC).

"We serve only one commissioner of the day, three deputy police commissioners, the ACPs, and down the line. Therefore, we must work together as a team," he added.

Supt Baim reminded officers to maintain professional pride, noting that public respect is earned through dedicated service.

"Take pride in your uniform, as that is the uniform that puts bread and butter on the table for your families. The public will respect the uniform that you wear. In return, you must give your best. This is the best job that you have in serving the people, and the Government pays you to look after its people," the PPC said.

He further challenged junior members of the force to consider their long-term legacy and contribution to the country's law enforcement sector over the coming decades.

"Some of us standing here today will not see the next 50 years. However, you as young officers must learn as much as you can from us. Ask yourselves what you can contribute to the development of Papua New Guinea in the next 50 years," he said.

Meanwhile, Supt Baim confirmed that a new vehicle fleet for the command has arrived in Lae.

The fleet was co-funded on a kina-for-kina basis by the Madang Provincial Government and the RPNGC.

While police had aimed to deploy the vehicles in time for the independence festivities, final administrative and mechanical clearances by supplier Ela Motors remain pending prior to their release to Madang.

item.title: Gang targeted in law and order funding
item.description: Northern governor Garry Juffa has escalated the fight against organized gangs, committing K6 million to law and order initiatives across the province. From this, K1 million was released today to launch the Provincial Police Command Reserve Training Program, which will recruit 100 reserve officers to reinforce frontline policing in hotspot areas where the notorious 'I Don’t Care Gang' is most activ
item.content:encoded:
Northern governor Garry Juffa has escalated the fight against organized gangs, committing K6 million to law and order initiatives across the province.

From this, K1 million was released today to launch the Provincial Police Command Reserve Training Program, which will recruit 100 reserve officers to reinforce frontline policing in hotspot areas where the notorious 'I Don’t Care Gang' is most active.

Governor Juffa said the gang has been responsible for widespread chaos, forcing teachers and health workers to abandon rural posts in fear of violent attacks.

“We are very concerned in Northern Province about the rise of gangs such as the ‘I Don’t Care Gang’ and in Momase, the ‘Operation Burukim Tulait’ gang. These groups are organized, they communicate, and they carry out violent attacks on our communities,” Juffa said.

The Provincial Government has completed an assessment of gang activities and recommended to the National Executive Council [NEC] that these groups be declared terrorist organizations under the Counter-Terrorism Act.

“If we don’t act decisively, it will send the wrong signal and encourage the proliferation of such gangs in other provinces,” Juffa said.

Meanwhile, the reserve training program will prioritize Grade 12 school leavers and local residents, aiming to restore safety and dismantle criminal networks.

item.title: K10m cattle project to revive Western province livestock sector
item.description: A K10 million Pilot Cattle Project is set to spearhead the revival of the livestock industry in Western Province, following a commitment announced by newly appointed Minister for Livestock and Member for Delta Fly, Agena Gamai. The initiative was unveiled during minister Gamai's first official state visit to the province from September 11 to 13, accompanied by Livestock Development Corporation [LD
item.content:encoded:
A K10 million Pilot Cattle Project is set to spearhead the revival of the livestock industry in Western Province, following a commitment announced by newly appointed Minister for Livestock and Member for Delta Fly, Agena Gamai.

The initiative was unveiled during minister Gamai's first official state visit to the province from September 11 to 13, accompanied by Livestock Development Corporation [LDC] managing director Steven Yangis and senior technical officers.

Under the pilot project's initial phase, 200 cattle will be mobilized from the Launakalana ranch in Rigo, Central province, and transported to primary project sites, including Awaba, Kenewa, and Morehead. The funding allocation will cover essential infrastructure, including perimeter fencing, farm supplies, and direct technical support for local growers.

Prior to the rollout, LDC technical teams conducted field assessments across key locations in Awaba, Kenewa, Wasua, Oriomo, Morehead, and Weam, to evaluate land suitability for cattle ranges, potential abattoir sites, and Post-Entry Quarantine [PEQ] facilities.

Addressing local leaders and residents in Awaba, Gamai said the project will bring economic significance to the region.

"When I took office, I made it clear that Western Province would be my top priority," the minister said. "This industry was originally established by missionaries and once thrived here, particularly among the Gogodala people. I am here to rebuild it and restore confidence among our farmers."

The Ministry of Livestock will partner with the Fly River provincial government, district authorities, and local-level government [LLG] presidents to execute the project through community-based farmer cooperatives. A formal Memorandum of Understanding [MOU] outlining the inter-governmental framework is scheduled for signing shortly.

item.title: Tumbuna Pikinini festival passes cultural knowledge to next generation
item.description: The first-ever Tumbuna Pikinini Cultural Festival in Aroma Coast, Central Province, is giving elders and children a platform to pass cultural knowledge from one generation to the next. Held at Aroma Primary School from September 8 to 9, the festival brought together children from early childhood, elementary and primary schools across the 19 wards of Maopa.
item.content:encoded:
The first-ever Tumbuna Pikinini Cultural Festival in Aroma Coast, Central Province, is giving elders and children a platform to pass cultural knowledge from one generation to the next.

Held at Aroma Primary School from September 8 to 9, the festival brought together children from early childhood, elementary and primary schools across the 19 wards of Maopa.

Through traditional dances, music, bilum weaving, storytelling and cultural displays, elders shared their knowledge, customs and traditions with the younger generation.

The festival directors say the initiative is aimed at ensuring traditional practices, languages and cultural identity are not lost, but continue to live through the children.

National Cultural Commission representative Eugene Avediba said the festival demonstrated the importance of cultural education and intergenerational knowledge transfer.

"NCC is committed to supporting the festival, which will also serve as a lead-up event to the Maopa Levapuka Tovi Cultural Festival," he said.

The NCC has pledged K10,000 in funding, together with logistics and technical support.

Organisers hope the Tumbuna Pikinini Cultural Festival will become an annual event, strengthening cultural preservation and community pride by connecting the wisdom of elders with the next generation.

item.title: Parkop calls for visionary leadership ahead of 2027 polls
item.description: Governor of National Capital District and Social Democratic Party [SDP] leader Powes Parkop has called on Papua New Guinea’s political parties to focus on developing visionary leadership, credible policies, and practical solutions ahead of the 2027 General Elections. Speaking at the 6th Political Party Expo, Parkop acknowledged key dignitaries present, including Registrar of Political Parties Emma
item.content:encoded:
Governor of National Capital District and Social Democratic Party [SDP] leader Powes Parkop has called on Papua New Guinea’s political parties to focus on developing visionary leadership, credible policies, and practical solutions ahead of the 2027 General Elections.

Speaking at the 6th Political Party Expo, Parkop acknowledged key dignitaries present, including Registrar of Political Parties Emmanuel Pok, Administrative Services Minister Richard Masere, and United Nations Resident Coordinator Shalini Bahuguna.

On behalf of the SDP, Parkop congratulated the Integrity of Political Parties and Candidates Commission [IPPCC] for its 25 years of work in strengthening political parties and building the capacity of leaders across the country.

Established in 2011, the SDP has contested three national elections. Parkop said the party is now preparing for its fourth election, working alongside other political entities to improve its standing and parliamentary representation.

He encouraged parties to compete strongly during campaigns, but stressed that political differences must not prevent leaders from uniting for the nation's interest.

“The most important thing is that we must think about our country and our people and come together, no matter which party we belong to,” Parkop said.

The NCD governor added that the ultimate responsibility of political parties is to provide the direction, leadership, and inspiration needed to advance Papua New Guinea for current and future generations.
